questions.q: Why would two packages you want to install both raise a dependency conflict?
options: pip only allows two packages to be installed per environment
They both require incompatible version ranges of a shared sub-dependency, and no single version satisfies both
One of the package names is spelled incorrectly
Dependency conflicts only happen with packages from different registries
questions.explain: A common cause is two libraries each depending on a shared package (like httpx), but requiring version ranges that don't overlap — pip has no single version it can install that satisfies both.

questions.q: When pip's resolver hits a genuine version conflict between two requested packages, what does it do?
options: Installs the newest version of each package regardless of the conflict
Silently skips installing one of the two packages without telling you
Reports the conflict explicitly, naming the packages and the incompatible version requirements, instead of guessing
Deletes your virtual environment automatically
questions.explain: Modern pip's dependency resolver refuses to install a combination it can't satisfy; it reports exactly which packages and version ranges are in conflict so you can resolve it.

options: Scans the currently installed packages and reports any unmet or broken dependency requirements
Updates every installed package to its latest version
Creates a new virtual environment
Checks your internet connection before running pip install
questions.explain: pip check inspects the active environment's installed packages for consistency and flags anything with an unmet dependency, which is useful after installs that might have bypassed normal dependency resolution.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the most effective way to prevent most dependency conflicts from ever happening?
options: Never install more than one package total
Install every package with --no-deps
Only use packages with no dependencies of their own
Give each project (or each genuinely incompatible pair of tools) its own isolated virtual environment, rather than sharing one environment for everything
questions.explain: Most dependency conflicts arise from crowding unrelated tools into one shared environment. Isolating projects into separate virtual environments (Lesson 18) sidesteps the vast majority of these conflicts before they occur.

questions.q: If `package-b` is later updated by its maintainers to support a newer range of its `httpx` dependency, how does that typically help resolve a prior conflict with `package-a`?
options: It doesn't help; conflicts can never be resolved by upgrading
Upgrading package-b to that newer version may widen its accepted httpx range enough to overlap with package-a's requirement, letting pip find one httpx version that satisfies both
It would only make the conflict worse
Package maintainers are not allowed to change dependency ranges
questions.explain: Upgrading the stricter package is usually the first thing worth trying: maintainers regularly widen or shift their own dependency bounds in new releases, which can eliminate a previously conflicting range entirely.
